sections.html:
Everett is a small, dense Middlesex County city directly north of Boston, next to the Charlestown neighborhood. About 3.7 square miles hold 49,075 residents, roughly 14,364 people per square mile, so houses sit close together on small lots. Most of the housing is on tight streets near Broadway, with industrial land along the water.

People look for homes here to stay near downtown Boston without paying Boston, Cambridge or Somerville living costs, and the population has been climbing. Compact houses, two-families and triple-deckers are the norm.

2020 census measureEverett
Housing units18,208
Households17,211
Vacant units5.5 percent
Homeowner vacancy rate0.9 percent
Rental vacancy rate4.0 percent

Under one percent means almost no owner-occupied home sits empty, so a house priced and shown well tends to draw interest quickly.

Broadway, part of Route 99, is the main business street. MBTA bus routes converge at Everett Square, and a bus lane runs on Broadway from Glendale Square to Sweetser Circle. Route 16 crosses the southern part of the city and links to U.S. Route 1 and Interstate 93, which both run just outside the city limits.

The Orange Line stops at Wellington, just across the line in Medford, and the commuter rail stops in Chelsea. Buyers who commute into Boston care about this. If your lot has off-street parking, say so in the listing or when you ask for an offer.

Several large projects are reshaping the waterfront, and buyers will ask about them.

  • Encore Boston Harbor, the Wynn resort, opened on June 23, 2019.
  • The former Exxon tank site was sold for cleanup and redevelopment, starting with raising the land and adding apartment buildings near Route 16, and Exxon agreed to a deed restriction barring fossil fuel storage there.
  • A 700 megawatt, four-hour battery received approval from the Energy Facilities Siting Board.
  • MassDOT is designing a bike and pedestrian bridge from the Encore harborwalk to Somerville's Draw Seven park.
  • The New England Revolution have plans for a soccer stadium in the city.

Construction can mean noise and truck traffic near the Mystic River for years. None of it changes what your own house is worth on a given day, but you should be able to say what is going on nearby.

sections.h2: Is flooding a concern for an Everett house?
sections.html:
Everett is low-lying, at an average elevation of about 10 feet, with a long waterfront on the Mystic River. The redevelopment plan for the old tank site includes raising the land to avoid climate-related flooding.

Expect a lender or buyer to want your lot's flood zone, and expect an inspector to notice a basement that has been wet. Check the zone and keep repair and insurance records where you can find them.

Chapter 64D of the General Laws puts an excise tax on the deed. It is measured on the price, leaving out any loan that stays on the property. Your closing attorney calculates it.

Everett's fire department also has to certify your smoke and carbon monoxide alarms. Book the visit the moment a closing date exists. It costs a fee, and the state's fire services office advises not to wait. Replace tired alarms before the inspector shows up.

Everett property tax is billed separately from the sale. Where a Massachusetts community bills quarterly, installments usually fall on August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1, and an abatement request must be filed by the first one. Read your own bill for the exact dates.

Call the Everett assessors if you think your house is overvalued, and bring comparable sales. Any balance still owing is taken from your proceeds at the closing table, so get the number before you settle on a price.

sections.h2: Selling with tenants, liens or repairs
sections.html:
Many Everett owners hold a two-family or a three-decker where one unit is rented. Before you list, gather each lease, note the rent and the end date, and check that the permits for past work are in order. Tenants keep their rights through a sale, and showings need their cooperation.

Liens and unpaid balances come out at closing, so find them early. A house that needs repairs can be fixed and listed, or sold as is, and the right choice depends on how much money and time you have.

sections.h2: What are the ways to sell an Everett house?
sections.html:
You have three common routes: list, sell by owner, or take a cash offer. A cash sale tends to appeal when time matters or the house needs work.

  • A listing can reach many buyers but involves showings and repair requests.
  • A sale by owner saves a fee but puts the work on you.
  • A cash buyer takes the house as is and can close when you want.

Cash Home Buyers takes Everett houses in their current condition, including ones with tenants, liens or repair needs. Request an offer, set it beside your other options, and decide at your own pace.

sections.h2: Preparing the house and the file
sections.html:
Everett lots are small, so first impressions come from the street. Clear the entry, tidy the yard and the walkway, and fix anything a visitor sees right away, like a loose railing or a broken window. Inside, a clean, empty basement helps an inspector and a buyer see what is there.

Then build the file: deed, recent tax bills, permit records, leases, any repair receipts and the fire department certificate once you have it. A seller who can hand a buyer's attorney a folder in one afternoon often keeps a deal on schedule.

Closings in a city this dense often hinge on small items: a lien that needs a payoff letter, a tenant who needs notice, an inspection date that slipped. List each one on a single page with a date next to it. If you are working against a deadline, such as a move, an estate settlement or a mortgage that is behind, tell every party the date up front so they can plan around it. A cash sale gives you the most control over timing, while a listing depends on a buyer's lender and inspection schedule.

Insist on a written offer, and read who pays which closing costs. Confirm the closing date and ask whether the buyer needs financing or inspections first. Then call the assessors for your tax balance and the fire department for an inspection date, so you know your net before you say yes. If a number looks wrong, ask your closing attorney to check it. Compare at least two options, even if one is a simple listing estimate, and take your time reading the terms. A fair offer will still look fair after a night's sleep and a call to your attorney.

faqs.q: How many people live in Everett, MA?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 49,075 residents on about 3.7 square miles.
Middlesex County, directly north of Boston and next to the Charlestown neighborhood.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke detector inspection to sell in Everett?
faqs.a: Yes. Everett's fire department signs off on smoke and carbon monoxide alarms before a sale. Call when you have a date.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed excise tax on a Massachusetts sale?
faqs.a: It is levied on the deed under chapter 64D of the General Laws, measured by the price. Your purchase contract usually decides who pays, so check with your attorney.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Everett house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Either repair and list, or sell as is to a cash buyer. Compare repair cost and time with the offer.
